evidence_spans: It is also important to note that the peak temperature of damping in the current Snoek-type high-damping HEAs is approximately 100 K higher than that in traditional high-damping alloys ( [11] , [12] , [31] – [42] ).

Because of the high configuration entropy and severely distorted lattices of HEAs ( [50] ), atomic position switches of interstitials in these matrices are impeded by the high atomic-scale distortion fields ( [51] ).
This effect gives rise to the high activation temperatures and barrier energies for the interstitial reorientation steps and the resulting high-temperature damping capability.

source_evidence_spans: These interstitial atoms in the severely distorted matrices with complex chemical short-range orders result in high strengthening, large ductility, and good high-temperature damping properties.

question_variants.question: Is the 'as-cast' microstructure in the XRD and EBSD analysis representative of the bulk properties, or does it contain significant segregation?
question_variants.resolution_summary: XRD was used to identify phases in the as-cast state. The text states the ingots were remelted to ensure homogeneity, but does not explicitly quantify segregation or confirm if the as-cast microstructure analyzed represents the bulk without segregation.

answers.answer: Phase identification of the as-cast alloys was conducted by XRD, but the paper does not explicitly state the extent of segregation or confirm representativeness beyond the claim of homogeneity from remelting.
answers.measurement_outcome: Two peaks resolved at 710 and 798 K
answers.mechanism: Jumps of randomly distributed interstitial atoms
answers.boundary_limitation: Complexity in alloy composition makes complete peak deconvolution difficult; segregation level not quantified.
evidence_spans: For the base HEA, two peaks could be resolved at 710 and 798 K, respectively (see green and magenta curves in Fig. 5A ).
As there is no ordered interstitial complex in the base HEA, the two decomposed peaks probably originate from the jumps of the randomly distributed interstitial atoms.
The height of the two Snoek damping peaks is 0.014 and 0.006, respectively.

answers.answer: Ingot preparation involved remelting at least eight times to ensure chemical homogeneity, but this refers to the bulk ingot state before casting, not necessarily the as-cast microstructure's local segregation during analysis.
answers.boundary_limitation: Remelting ensures bulk homogeneity; local segregation in as-cast state not explicitly detailed in the context of XRD/EBSD representativeness.
evidence_spans: Alloy ingots with a nominal composition of Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi, (Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi) 98 O 2 , and (Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi) 98 N 2 (at %) were prepared by arc-melting a mixture of pure metals (purity, >99.9 weight %), TiN (99.9 weight %), and TiO 2 (99.9 weight %) in a Ti-gettered high-purity argon atmosphere.
The ingots were remelted at least eight times to ensure chemical homogeneity.
Melted alloys were eventually drop-cast into a water-cooled copper mold with a dimension of 10 mm by 10 mm by 60 mm.
